what_it_does: Copies the dx-toolkit Python source into a fresh temporary directory and runs the macOS test suite for one Python environment inside it.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The copy is a local 19 MB tree that is small next to the venv build and pip install that follow. run_tests.sh installs from that tree with pip, which can write build output into it, so one shared copy would race when workers is above 1.

what_it_does: Copies the source tree into a temporary directory, creates a venv there, and runs pytest for one Windows Python environment.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The copy is a local 19 MB tree, small next to the venv creation and pip install that follow. pip installs from that tree and can write build output into it, so each environment and each retry needs its own copy to avoid carrying state between runs.

what_it_does: Builds the Docker test image for one Python environment, pulling the base image first, and writes the build log to disk.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Pulling is the default and the documented behaviour, and --no-docker-pull exists to turn it off, so the repair would change which base image gets tested. Each pull is one registry manifest check against a full image build, so the saving is small.

what_it_does: Installs each requested pyenv or brew Python version in turn, runs the per-environment test workers, and writes the execution summary.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Dropping the force flag changes what brew does to a broken or unlinked formula, and a skip changes the output written to the install log at line 106 on every run. The energy saved is real, but the repair changes machine state and logged output, so it is rejected.

what_it_does: Writes a local test file, either 100 MB of random bytes or the given text, uploads it with dx upload, and polls dx describe until the file is closed.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The wait is needed because dx upload without --wait returns while the file is still closing, so the loop normally makes a few polls. Passing --wait would move the wait into one process with backoff, but the failure path would change: today it raises an AssertionError after about 200 seconds, while the repair would wait up to a day inside dx and print different error text.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: Random content is generated in one test call at line 168, and the kernel took about half a second to produce 100 MB here, which is small beside the 100 MB upload that follows. Writing zeros would change the uploaded bytes for a saving too small to justify that change.

what_it_does: Logs a pass or fail line for each environment, optionally writes the results to a JSON report, and returns the overall exit code.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The list is built once per summary over at most 21 entries, so replacing it with a generator saves nothing measurable.

what_it_does: Returns a urllib3 connection pool that is cached for default settings, and builds a fresh uncached pool on every call when verify, cert_file, key_file, ssl_context or DX_CA_CERT is set.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each uncached call builds a new pool, so every request opens a new TCP connection and TLS handshake. A single-slot cache keyed on verify, cert_file, key_file, ssl_context, DX_CA_CERT, DX_USE_OS_CA_BUNDLE and the proxy variable reuses the pool, the proxy message still prints on every call, and the error path clear call at line 727 then acts on the pool that was used, which is what that call intends.

what_it_does: Walks the resources directory, computes a checksum from file metadata, reuses a matching bundle if one exists, and otherwise tars, gzips and uploads the tree.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The checksum uses only stat data, yet the code reads and writes every resource file into an uncompressed tar before it looks for a matching bundle. The repair runs a metadata-only first walk that opens each regular file, never a FIFO, so an unreadable file still raises the same error before any lookup, and it builds the archive only when no bundle matches, so the reuse path skips every content read and tar write.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The finished uncompressed tar is re-read in 8 KB chunks and gzipped into a second temp file, which costs one full write and one full read of the archive on the upload path. Writing the gzip stream directly with tarfile in w:gz mode gives the same tar entries at compression level 9, so only the gzip header timestamp and temp file name differ, as they already do between runs.

what_it_does: Creates or updates an app version from its spec, syncs its categories, developers and authorized users, and publishes it or tags it as the default.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The authorized-user list at line 900 is needed when the spec has authorizedUsers or when brief is False. With brief True and no authorizedUsers its result is unused, but a failure of that call raises today, so skipping it would silence an error on an input the current code accepts, and the saving is one read-only request per brief build.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The next form returns the same boolean, but list() requests a second page only when the search reports more results, so the repair also removes a request whose failure raises today. That is the same kind of change as line 900, and the saving is one request for apps with two or more published versions.

what_it_does: Uploads the asset config, makefile and tarball, starts the asset builder job, waits for it to finish, and prints the resulting asset ID.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The job is polled with a describe once per second for the whole build. An interval of 10 seconds gives the same return value and the same failure path, cuts state requests about tenfold, and adds at most ten seconds at the end of the build.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The call is the credential check that runs before any upload, so removing it changes which call fails first and the text printed for a bad token, which would then come from dx_upload. The saving is one request per asset build.

what_it_does: Returns the billTo for a build, defaulting to the caller's own billTo and checking that a user or org value is allowed.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: For an org billTo the user id is not used, so the whoami call could move, but the org_describe call sits inside a bare except. With an invalid token today the DXAPIError from whoami propagates, while the repair would turn the same auth failure into the builder exception, so the exception type changes.

what_it_does: Checks the executables of each workflow stage, recursing into inner workflows, and narrows the set of regions in which the workflow can be enabled.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each applet stage describes its project and that project's region again, and each app stage describes the same app again, so every repeated stage costs one request. A memo keyed on executable and project id, passed through the recursion with a None default, returns the same values, and the first failing describe still raises as before.

what_it_does: Lists every notebook app version and returns each version string by describing each app separately.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The loop makes one app describe per version just to read the version string. A find_apps call with describe set returns that field inside the search that already runs, and utils/completer.py already reads result['describe'] from find_apps, so the list is the same and the per-app requests go away, provided the search describe includes version on the platform.

what_it_does: Polls the job every 5 seconds until the notebook server tag appears or the job fails, then exits with advice if it failed.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each poll fetches the full job description, including inputs and outputs that the loop never reads. Asking only for state and tags keeps the loop, the request count and the failure message unchanged, so each poll sends and parses a smaller payload, which is a small saving, and the platform must accept those field names.

what_it_does: Returns the message unchanged if its JSON form fits in 8015 characters, otherwise cuts it to a JSON-safe prefix with a truncation marker.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The trim runs json.dumps once per byte removed, up to about 4000 times for non-ASCII or escape-heavy text, but the 8000 byte slice at line 77 caps the cost, so the cost is bounded and not quadratic in message size. A binary search over the prefix length returned identical output on 400 random inputs that I checked, and it cut a 12000 character CJK message from 0.11 s to 0.4 ms.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The whole message is encoded and serialised once just to measure it, which is linear in the message and costs a few microseconds for typical records. That is too small to justify an edit to a logging path.

what_it_does: Looks up each cacheable image reference in the project image cache, sets its file ID on a hit, and prints one progress line per reference.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Duplicate references repeat an identical find_data_objects search, one request per process that uses the image. A memo keyed on cache folder, cache file name and digest, storing only successful results, lets each reference still set its file ID and print its line, and failed lookups stay unmemoized so their warnings repeat as before; the existing test at test_nextflow_collect_images.py line 336 asserts two calls and would need to assert one.

what_it_does: Runs docker manifest inspect with up to two retries after 60 and 300 seconds, and returns the parsed JSON or None.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The sleeps are idle time, which costs little energy, and each retry adds one more docker manifest inspect run, which is a registry request. The retries exist for transient registry and network errors, and a no-retry repair would turn those into a None digest for a valid image, so the behaviour changes.

what_it_does: Starts the Nextflow importer job, waits for it to finish by polling once per second, and returns the applet ID.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The importer job is polled with a describe once per second until it finishes. An interval of 10 seconds gives the same applet ID and the same failure path, cuts state requests about tenfold, and adds at most ten seconds at the end of the import.

what_it_does: Tars the app directory, uploads the archive, starts the remote builder job, optionally watches it, waits for it to finish, and returns the applet ID.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: With watch off, the remote build job is polled once per second, and an app build runs for minutes. An interval of 10 seconds keeps the return value and the failure path and cuts state requests about tenfold, at the cost of up to ten seconds of latency.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The loop spins only between the end of tar's stdout and tar being reaped, since read blocks while data flows, so the spin lasts about as long as tar takes to exit. That window is normally very short, and a sleep would add latency for little energy gain.

what_it_does: Returns the bundledDepends entry for one image, caching it on the platform when no file ID is known and otherwise describing the existing file to get its name.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The describe at line 93 is needed because the name is not kept on the _ImageRef record, so removing the call means carrying the name through the collect_docker_images output. That changes the documented return keys of that function, and the saving is one describe per cache hit.
